source.title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
source.authors: Meng-Ying Zhang; De-Rui Wang; Ibrahim Khalil; Bo-Wen Liu; Xiao-Yu Xia; Min-Hui Xue

page_placements.theme: Reconstruction of forgotten data from pre- and post-unlearning checkpoints

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether text targeted by approximate unlearning remains recoverable, using a data-free reconstruction attack on paired pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots. This is a different recovery mechanism from the specific attacks in claim versions A–F.
record.gate_note: The study reports reconstruction outcomes from TRACE and a PPL-only comparator, including results after checkpoint quantization, post-unlearning fine-tuning, and exact retraining. These results bear on general post-unlearning recoverability, but do not test the specific behaviors named in versions A–F. Parameter differences used to construct TRACE’s candidate-token set are part of the attack, not a result that unlearning deletes or blocks access to knowledge.
record.test_reason: TRACE reconstructs forgotten training text by contrasting the pre- and post-unlearning snapshots. The signal comes from the pre-unlearning model's memorization plus the perplexity gap. The study never measures whether the unlearned model itself still holds or yields the targeted knowledge under fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization or prompting. This is a different construct: cross-snapshot data leakage, not recovery of hidden knowledge. The record's 'tests'/T2 contradicts its own 'not_tested' status for every version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Add that exact retraining still allows about 5% exact reconstruction, and that pruning reduces reconstruction but also undoes unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests TRACE, a data-free cross-snapshot text-reconstruction attack, rather than the listed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization-as-recovery, or prompting attacks. It also evaluates six unlearning methods as targets.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction varies with model, unlearning method, dataset, unlearning batch size, pre-unlearning training epochs, white-box versus black-box access, and checkpoint transformations. The text specifically reports lower reconstruction in black-box access, reduced reconstruction after exact retraining, and partial reduction after increasing the post-unlearning fine-tuning set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Given pre- and post-unlearning snapshots, TRACE reconstructs forgotten text without priors. TOFU A-ESR1.0 is 61–96% across 5 models and 6 methods. Exact retraining cuts this to 5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate unlearning leaves cross-snapshot parameter traces that allow data-free reconstruction of the forgotten text.

fits_no_version.finding: Wanda pruning at 50% of the NPO-unlearned LLaMA2-7B lowers forget-sample perplexity from 16.07 to 5.07. The authors say pruning compromises the effect of unlearning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight pruning of an unlearned model can partly undo unlearning on the forget set. This is a compression-based analogue of D.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The threat model requires access to pre- and post-unlearning snapshots; the main setting has white-box parameter access. Results use benchmark datasets and the reported reconstruction attack rather than the recovery mechanisms specified in the claim versions. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the main results, which are averaged over 10 randomly sampled batches. The paper notes that effectiveness depends on memorization strength and unlearning batch size.
record.rows_left_out: The main tables also report ROUGE-L and A-ESR0.9, and the paper includes additional MUSE, batch-size, hyperparameter-sensitivity, pruning, and parameter-obfuscation results. These are not all transcribed as separate rows; the 60-row limit is not reached, but the retained rows prioritize the exact-match reconstruction results across all TOFU models and unlearning methods, plus the distinct post-unlearning transformation and retraining comparisons. Some MUSE table entries are flattened without sufficient method-column alignment in the provided text, so they were not assigned to individual methods.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy with general ability kept, and resistance to simple attacks, are not measured.
No relearning attack on the unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation, and no analysis of blocking access versus deleting knowledge.
Forget-set behaviour after quantization is not measured.
No robust unlearning method is proposed. Only heuristic defenses against TRACE are evaluated.

missing.what: Forget-sample perplexity under Wanda pruning at 0/10/30/50%: 16.07, 17.50, 13.58, 5.07. This is the one result on the unlearned model's own forget-set behaviour after compression.
missing.versions: none (closest to D, but pruning rather than quantization)

record.verdict_notes: WMDP is used only as a long-form text corpus (bio-retain-corpus), not for hazardous-knowledge accuracy. The study is not an original source. No verdicts are given because no row measures the unlearned model's retained knowledge.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy while preserving general ability, or test whether simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge.
Does not fine-tune an unlearned model on a small relearning set to restore targeted knowledge. Its post-unlearning fine-tuning experiment measures TRACE reconstruction performance.
Does not ablate an activation direction or establish that an unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Applies quantization to an unlearned checkpoint and measures TRACE reconstruction, not whether quantization restores the model’s targeted-knowledge behavior.
Does not test rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.
Evaluates heuristic defenses against TRACE, not a newer method resisting the attacks specified in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: No version is tested. The study attacks approximate unlearning in a different way (snapshot-based text reconstruction) and discusses the privacy risk it leaves.

tranche.reason: TRACE reconstructs forgotten text using both the pre- and post-unlearning snapshots. Its signal comes from the original model's memorization plus the perplexity gap. It does not test whether the unlearned model alone still holds the knowledge under the recovery attacks the versions name. The reader's T2 is a stretch. The one loosely related side result, Wanda pruning in Table 7, fits no version.

source_check.notes: All 25 Table 1 TOFU rows match the text (B=8, 10 sampled batches). Exact retraining (5% A-ESR1.0) is MUSE-only, probably TinyLlama. Side result not in the rows (Table 7): 50% Wanda pruning of NPO-unlearned LLaMA2-7B on MUSE lowers forget-sample PPL from 16.07 to 5.07. The authors say it compromises unlearning; no pre-unlearning PPL is given. The 4-bit AWQ test (Table 6) measures only TRACE, so version D is untested. The pack covers 25 of 42 rows.

statements.correction: TOFU A-ESR1.0 (Table 1, B=8, mean of 10 batches) runs from 61.25% (Mistral-7B, KL) to 96.25% (LLaMA2-7B NPO-KL; LLaMA2-13B NPO). Exact retraining (App. D.5, Table 12): MUSE only, B=8, 4 training epochs, A-ESR1.0 5.00%. Compared with NPO 51.25% white-box and 27.50% black-box. D.5 names no model; its NPO values match Table 5's TinyLlama 4-epoch column.
statements.problem: The TOFU A-ESR1.0 range of 61-96% over 5 models x 6 methods is right. But 'exact retraining cuts this to 5%' ties the 5% to TOFU. It comes from one MUSE run (App. D.5, Table 12) compared with NPO's 51.25%, so it says nothing about the TOFU numbers.
